term: that than which nothing greater can be thought
definition: Anselm's description of God (Proslogion 2): a being than which no greater can be conceived. It is a modal and conceptual notion, not a maximum among the beings found in things.
note: Analyst parameterized formulation; attribution deferred, with Proslogion 2 retained only as navigation, not a new source claim. NoGreaterConceivable T s b means b is conceivable and every conceivable x is not Greater than b. Conceivable supplies an accessible possible-thought situation and an entertainable concept intentionally denoting the candidate. Situation, Concept and Being are separate carriers. Accessibility is possible thought scope, not metaphysical possibility; CanEntertain is capacity, not an actual episode; Denotes is intentional reference, not actual realization. Greater is primitive comparative greatness of objects as conceived, with no totality, asymmetry, uniqueness or order alignment assumed. OPEN semantic dictionaries: which thought situations are admissible, which concepts can be entertained, what they intentionally denote, and which comparative greatness is intended. A conceived golden mountain can be represented without realization; an unentertainable description is excluded. Concrete application to God remains open. Own conceivability excludes empty-scope vacuity. Incomparability permits multiple no-greater candidates. toMaximal uses one carrier B both for the intentional objects of Thought and for the InAct/MoreIn domain of actual perfection bearers; this carrier identification of conceived object with actual bearer is an OPEN analyst identification, not a consequence of Denotes. Given it, toMaximal connects to the exact quarta-via IsMaximalIn only under separately supplied actual possession, coverage of every MoreIn competitor, and one-way comparison alignment. Actual-only coverage needs the further dictionary that every MoreIn competitor is actual, because IsMaximalIn has an unguarded comparison clause.
